evidence.exact_quote: Cleanup actions, retained artifacts, evidence, and manual Clean workspace activity are first-class artifacts/events in the unified event model, with redb carrying retention policy, retention metadata, and rollups while cleanup boundaries align to patch/apply/verify/rollback rather than UI-only affordances.

Cleanup implementation proceeds in DRY-friendly order: create src/cleanup, centralize the allowlist and run_git_clean_with_excludes, implement prepare and cleanup functions, add the run_with_cleanup wrapper and call-site adoption, then add agent-output, evidence pruning, and manual Clean workspace behavior.

Cleanup UX changes use existing widgets, provide Expert and ELI5 copy variants for authored tooltip/help/discoverability copy, let app-level Interaction Mode choose the displayed variant, and keep Chat ELI5 separate and chat-only.

items.impact: The architecture and sequencing are explicit, but the event payload/rollup schema and the actual paired Expert/ELI5 copy corpus are not defined here, leaving interoperable storage and copy-completeness decisions to builders and weakening exact acceptance tests.
items.statement: M-002 through M-004 establish cleanup as an event-backed, DRY-sequenced subsystem with widget reuse and Interaction Mode copy separation. Adversarially, they do not enumerate the event schema, rollup invariants, or a complete copy matrix, so two conforming builders could emit incompatible events or materially different GUI explanations while passing the lineage-only acceptance criteria.
items.title: Cleanup event architecture is explicit but its payload and copy oracles are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: Target project AGENTS.md may be seeded with DRY Method and technology/version constraints from the interview, but implementation ownership remains with interview-subagent-integration.md §5.1 and agents_md_generator.

Cleanup never removes state files, .puppet-master except explicitly allowed pruning, config/discovery paths, .gitignore, sensitive credential patterns, or the headless GUI evidence path; agent-output may be cleared only by policy while preserving the rest of .puppet-master.

Assistant-owned worktrees identified by owner_thread_id are persistent by default; chat header Remove, thread delete, Source Control row Remove, Doctor orphan cleanup, app uninstall, and completed-thread behavior each have explicit cleanup semantics and confirmations.

Cleanup runs only in the actual selected main repo, worktree, lane, attempt workspace, or worktree path used by the agent, and must not clean the main working tree for artifacts owned by another lane, attempt, or worktree.

Cleanup supports conservative, moderate, and configurable modes, with operator-controlled untracked, clean_ignored, clear_agent_output, remove_build_artifacts, and skip_prepare_for_conversation fields and conservative defaults that avoid aggressive cleanup unless configured.

The src/cleanup module owns cleanup policy and execution; reusable cleanup functions, helpers, and data are DRY-tagged, parent module declaration is explicit, and pre-implementation checks prevent duplicate cleanup logic.

items.impact: These contracts materially constrain destructive behavior: ownership is handed off explicitly, protected paths and credential patterns are centralized, worktree persistence is user-confirmed, cleanup is lane/attempt isolated, and aggressive modes are opt-in.
items.statement: M-005 through M-010 form a coherent safety boundary: interview owns AGENTS generation, MiscPlan owns centralized cleanup policy, assistant worktrees persist by default, cleanup targets only the run's selected workspace, modes default conservatively, and duplicated allowlists or git-clean logic are forbidden. The adversarial destructive-action, cross-lane, secret-path, and ownership-confusion cases are directly constrained rather than silently delegated.
items.title: Cleanup protection, isolation, and DRY ownership form a strong non-gap

evidence.exact_quote: Git operations respect .gitignore, never introduce git add -f for paths that could be secrets, optionally guard staged sensitive files, and never log, commit, capture in evidence, or include in GitHub content tokens, keys, or credential file contents.

run_git_clean_with_excludes is the only git-clean helper, reads cleanup_exclude_patterns from the cleanup module, emits one -e per exclude pattern, uses shared git binary resolution, and is called only by prepare_working_directory or manual Clean workspace.

prepare_working_directory performs a best-effort git repo check, skips rather than fails non-repo or git-unavailable cases, does not reset tracked files without a future explicit config, runs broad untracked cleanup only before execution, and may clear agent-output in prepare.

cleanup_after_execution terminates the process if needed, removes runner temp files, may remove known build-artifact directories by config, and must not run broad untracked cleanup after execution because that would delete current-run outputs before commit.

The canonical implementation uses run_with_cleanup around runner.execute; orchestrator, research, and start-chain paths must adopt it, conversation is optional/project-aware, config is passed into execution paths, and PlatformRunner keeps only execute with earlier trait-extension wording retained as compatibility lineage.

.puppet-master/agent-output/ is the disposable scratch area; its path is DRY data, optional run subdirectories may be used, contents may be cleared only in prepare_working_directory, and STATE_FILES.md plus AGENTS.md document the behavior.

items.impact: A hung or child-spawning runner can produce inconsistent cleanup if termination escalation, descendants, wait limits, and failure propagation differ by caller; silent best-effort prepare skips can also make a run appear protected when cleanup never occurred.
items.statement: M-011 through M-016 correctly centralize secret-safe git handling, before/after boundaries, wrapper adoption, and agent-output clearing. The exact contract is incomplete for process-tree termination, escalation timeout, cleanup error precedence, and the observable state of best-effort prepare skips; exhaustive caller adoption is stated but no machine-checkable caller inventory/oracle is supplied.
items.title: Runner cleanup lacks complete termination, skip, and caller-adoption oracles

evidence.exact_quote: Evidence lifecycle aligns to seglog and redb; retention is configurable by days or runs, pruning is scheduled/manual and outside the hot cleanup_after_execution path, and current or in-progress run evidence must not be deleted when feasible.
Evidence retention and pruning documentation must tell users that evidence can be pruned and must warn agents not to rely on very old evidence paths.
Cleanup and evidence settings must be modeled in one run/config schema with deterministic defaults and must be projected from the same GuiConfig/config path used by the rest of the app.

Cleanup and evidence controls must be visible inside the existing Advanced config surface, preferably as a Workspace / Cleanup subsection, using existing GUI catalog widgets and the same GuiConfig projection path as other run settings.

Clean workspace now must run prepare-style workspace cleanup for the intended project path, with confirmations, optional dry-run/evidence pruning, clear feedback, and disabled-state safety when no project context exists.

Cleanup GUI wiring must align with Worktree, Orchestrator, Interview, Providers, and Source Control owner surfaces without collapsing per-project, per-worktree, or historical lineage state into a single global cleanup pool.

items.impact: Concurrent pruning can destroy active evidence if run activity and atomicity are interpreted differently; users may also see divergent control placement because the Advanced-crowding fallback and accessibility/localization expectations have no deterministic trigger or oracle.
items.statement: M-017 through M-022 establish one config projection, manual-clean safety, documentation, partitioned GUI state, and out-of-hot-path pruning. The phrase 'when feasible' leaves current/in-progress evidence protection non-normative; retain-last-runs ordering, active-run detection, prune concurrency/atomicity, partial deletion recovery, and the objective threshold for moving controls to a ninth tab remain unspecified.
items.title: Evidence pruning races and cleanup-control placement remain underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: Platform hooks, skills, plugins, extensions, and MCP integrations can complement cleanup and agent context, but Puppet Master prepare/cleanup remains an internal run_with_cleanup responsibility and is not dependent on provider-native extension mechanisms.
Cursor provider bootstrap/trust status copy must preserve the exact title and subtext specified by the source span.

A Shortcuts GUI surface must show the complete default shortcut table, current bindings, change/double-click edit flow, reset controls, persistence, widget reuse, and immediate reflection of the active key map.

Shortcut handling must use a single registry of actions/defaults, serializable KeyBinding overrides in GuiConfig, a DRY build_key_map merge function, platform-aware display/mapping, and deterministic rebuild/install timing for all focusable text areas.

Shortcut editing/import must reject or explicitly resolve duplicate bindings, recover from invalid shortcut config with defaults and a toast, distinguish empty filters from no matches, and avoid blank or undefined labels while the key map is loading.

The Shortcuts surface must support export/import of overrides, Replace/Merge confirmation, list filtering by action or key, menu/tooltip shortcut labels, and shared DRY helper functions that reuse GuiConfig shortcut serialization.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree on where Shortcuts lives, whether import/export represents overrides or a full map, how unknown actions and versions behave, and whether key-map replacement is atomic across open inputs; those differences can make displayed bindings diverge from active behavior or permit partial state after failure.
items.statement: M-023 and M-024 precisely separate internal cleanup responsibility from provider extensions and provide exact Cursor copy oracles. M-025 through M-028 define a shared shortcut registry, visible active bindings, conflict/config recovery, and import/export. Adversarially, the canonical UI location is intentionally unchosen, 'all focusable text areas' lacks a closed registry, replace/merge transaction boundaries are not explicit, and reject-versus-steal, unknown-action, unknown-version, and overrides-versus-full-map choices remain builder discretion.
items.title: Shortcut contracts are rich but location, scope, and atomic import behavior remain open

evidence.exact_quote: A Skills management GUI surface must exist for discover/list/add/edit/remove/permissions behavior, while final placement follows the current Skills/GUI owner docs and older Config/Settings placement wording is retained as source lineage compatibility.

Skill discovery and validation must follow the one-folder-per-skill SKILL.md package model, ordered project/global discovery roots, strict OpenCode-aligned name validation, frontmatter requirements, and required_tool_refs/optional_tool_refs readiness semantics.

Skill loading is permission-gated through permission.skill, Persona default_skill_refs and permission profiles, available_skills tool descriptions, skill({ name }) on-demand retrieval, /skillname commands, external_directory allowlisting, and compaction preservation.

The Skills GUI must list discovered skills with source and permission state, support create/import/edit/remove/permission/refresh flows, refresh only on open/mutations/manual refresh, and surface frontmatter, missing SKILL.md, and config-write errors without corrupting state.

PM-native skill runtime delivery must compute readiness from validation, permission, and tool availability; bundle selected skill content into compiled context; expose the PM skill tool for on-demand retrieval; and avoid requiring provider-native runtime delivery matrices for MVP.

Skill import/discovery can read compatible roots, but projection/export is optional and explicit, tracked per projection target, separated between workspace-owned and provider-root-owned state, and direct edits move only the chosen target to Manual Override.

items.impact: Ambiguous precedence and non-atomic mutation handling could load a denied skill, misstate readiness, lose edits after disk/config races, or confuse projection failure with runtime failure despite the explicit ownership separation.
items.statement: M-029 through M-034 define package validation, permission-gated loading, GUI mutations, PM-native readiness, and per-target projection drift boundaries. The exact cross-layer precedence among Persona defaults, explicit skill rules, wildcard rules, and runtime asks is spread across units rather than expressed as one total decision table; edit/import/remove/config-write operations also lack a complete transaction and concurrent-disk-change state machine, while final surface placement is delegated to owner docs.
items.title: Skills core needs a total permission decision table and transactional mutation model

evidence.exact_quote: Skills implementation planning must preserve the resolved gaps table covering first-wins discovery deduplication, create-no-overwrite behavior, concurrent-edit handling recommendation, full validate-all status table, deferred ask timing, import-copy semantics, global-only create without a project, and name/folder match enforcement.

The Skills tab must support a bulk permission pattern control where users enter a wildcard pattern, select Allow/Deny/Ask, confirm the matched count, persist GuiConfig.skill_permissions, and preserve explicit per-skill precedence over patterns.
Skills bulk-permission updates must route through shared backend permission state, report config-persist failures, and leave retryable in-memory state instead of pretending unsaved changes succeeded.
The Skills tab must support in-memory sort and combined filters over the discovered skill list without re-running discovery on sort or filter changes.
The Skills tab must provide an on-demand read-only SKILL.md body preview with copyable text and clear per-skill load errors.

Skill list and preview metadata must show last-modified information and may show optional version metadata when supported, while unreadable mtimes degrade to an empty or placeholder value without dropping the skill.

items.impact: Without explicit snapshot invalidation and retry-state rules, bulk permission counts can be stale, saved and unsaved permissions can be visually conflated, preview metadata can refer to a replaced file, and large skill sets can incur unbounded in-memory filtering or validation costs.
items.statement: M-035 through M-040 preserve important decisions for deduplication, no-overwrite creation, ask timing, pattern precedence, retryable save failure, in-memory controls, on-demand preview, and mtime degradation. Adversarially, the units do not define snapshot/version binding between discovery, bulk match confirmation, persist retry, preview load, and metadata display, and they provide no explicit scale bounds or accessible/localized behavior for large tables and error states.
items.title: Advanced Skills flows need snapshot consistency, scale, and retry-state oracles

segments.summary: Reviewed the cleanup event model, DRY implementation order, and Interaction Mode copy/widget contracts; principal gap is the absence of concrete event payload/rollup and complete copy acceptance oracles.

Reviewed AGENTS seeding ownership, protected-path policy, assistant-worktree persistence, lane/worktree isolation, cleanup modes, and centralized DRY ownership; these are explicit safety contracts rather than negative-space gaps.

Reviewed secret-safe git behavior, the sole git-clean helper, prepare/after boundaries, wrapper caller adoption, and agent-output clearing; termination escalation, skip observability, cleanup error precedence, and exhaustive caller proof remain incomplete.

Reviewed evidence retention/docs, unified config projection, Advanced placement, manual clean safety, and cross-owner partitioning; active-evidence pruning races and deterministic GUI fallback criteria remain gaps.

Reviewed provider non-dependency, exact Cursor trust copy, and the complete Shortcuts registry/edit/import/filter family; canonical location, closed input scope, atomic import, and several compatibility choices are still open.

Reviewed Skills surface ownership, package discovery/validation, permissions, GUI CRUD, PM-native runtime readiness, and projection drift; total permission precedence and transactional mutation states are not closed.

Reviewed resolved Skills decisions, bulk permissions/save recovery, sort/filter, body preview, and modified/version metadata; snapshot consistency, retry-state presentation, accessibility/localization, and scale limits remain underspecified.

cross_document_questions: Which owner contract supplies the normative process-tree termination, escalation timeout, and cleanup-error precedence for cleanup_after_execution?
